newsitem.title: USA: Flagstar restructuring may be imminent - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Flagstar restructuring may be imminent - analysts.

text.p: Several Wall Street analysts said there is a strong chance Flagstar Cos Inc will begin restructuring its heavy debt load next week by possibly defaulting on $21.6 million in interest payments due on its bonds.

"We expect Flagstar to miss its March 15 interest payment and begin restructuring negotiations with its bondholders," wrote Chris Kane and Neal Goldman, two distressed debt analysts at Salomon Brothers Inc, in a recent research report.

Flagstar is in discussions with a group of senior subordinated bondholders regarding a possible restructuring, according to an official at Houlihan Lokey Howard & Zukin. Houlihan Lokey has been hired by the bondholder group as a financial advisor.
A spokeswoman for Flagstar declined any comment on the interest payments or negotiations with bondholders.

Flagstar, one of the largest restaurant companies in the U.S., announced in January that it was exploring options to restructure its debt and hired Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp as an advisor.

"We believe that a restructuring will be fairly straightforward, and that a pre-arranged or pre-packaged bankruptcy will be the preferred method to accomplish the deleveraging," the Salomon analysts added.
David Goldburg, head of bankruptcy research at Bear Stearns & Co Inc, also believed a pre-packaged bankruptcy plan was likely.
"The company has way too much debt. It's pretty clear on paper that Flagstar should equitize its subordinated bonds. That shouldn't take too much time to implement," said Goldburg.
Following Flagstar's January announcement, Moody's Investors Service Inc and Standard & Poor's cut their ratings on Flagstar Corp's senior notes to Caa/CCC and its subordinated notes to Ca/CCC-minus.
S&P stated, "Flagstar continues to have weak credit protection measures, mostly reflecting a very high debt burden and difficulties in improving operations at its various restaurants."
On March 15, Flagstar must make interest payments of $14.5 million on outstanding senior notes and $7.1 million on outstanding subordinated notes.
Flagstar owns several large restaurant chains, including Denny's, Hardee's, and Quincy's.
